## Description
 &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;The defining feature of all polyurethanes is the urethane linkage (carbamate group).  &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;The general formula for the repeating unit in the polymer chain is:&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;[–R–NH–CO–O–R&#39;–O–]ₙ&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;Where:&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;1. –NH–CO–O– is the urethane linkage formed during the reaction. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;2. R represents the organic structure derived from the isocyanate (e.g., aromatic &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   rings from MDI or TDI), containing the reactive –N&#61;C&#61;O group. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   - MDI (Methylene Diphenyl Diisocyanate): 250.25 g/mol (Formula: C₁₅H₁₀N₂O₂).  &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;     This is the most common isocyanate for rigid foams and elastomers.&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   - TDI (Toluene Diisocyanate): 174.16 g/mol (Formula: C₉H₆N₂O₂).  &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;     Primarily used in flexible foams. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   - H₁₂MDI (Hydrogenated MDI): 262.35 g/mol.  Used for weather-resistant coatings.   &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;3. R&#39;, the soft segment, represents the organic structure derived from the polyol &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   (e.g., polyether or polyester chains). &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   - Chain Extenders: Very low molecular weight diols (e.g., 1,4-Butanediol at &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;     90.12 g/mol or Ethylene Glycol at 62.07 g/mol) are often added to link hard segments. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;4. n indicates the number of repeating units, which can be very large.&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;
